Adding the infra notes I promised. See key tradeoffs below (also in infra_comparison_table.xlsx):

- Hosted (fastest time-to-value): 1-2 days onboarding, full feature parity, limited dedicated throughput guarantees. Recommended if initial throughput < 50 rps and PHI encrypted in transit + at rest with Redwood KMS.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools; lead time ~4 weeks (provisioning + warm-up). Best for sustained >=50 rps with medium-latency SLOs. Can optionally provision in US-West with failover to US-East.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation, customer-managed keys, compliance-friendly; lead time 6-8 weeks and additional ops runbook required.

Decision matrix suggestion for Cinder:
- If latency requirement <= 120ms p50 and bursty traffic: Hosted with autoscaling + prefix caching.
- If consistent peak throughput > 60 rps or strict isolation: Dedicated commit.
- If data residency + on-prem required by legal: Private.

I attached a short security_faq.pdf that maps our evidence to common questionnaire asks.

Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
